source: M6 14 (the every-spell rule; the owner, 2026-11-16: she buys every spell, eventually, when affordable): every scroll the catalog's scriveners (scriveners.json $.scriveners, the 40 weenies) sell, read from the read-only world copy on 2026-11-16: SELECT d.value, s.name, cl.weenie_Class_Id, v.value, b.value, cl.object_Id, cl.id FROM weenie_properties_create_list cl JOIN weenie_properties_int it ON it.object_Id = cl.weenie_Class_Id AND it.type = 1 AND it.value = 8192 JOIN weenie_properties_d_i_d d ON d.object_Id = cl.weenie_Class_Id AND d.type = 28 LEFT JOIN spell s ON s.id = d.value LEFT JOIN weenie_properties_int v ON v.object_Id = cl.weenie_Class_Id AND v.type = 19 LEFT JOIN weenie_properties_int b ON b.object_Id = cl.weenie_Class_Id AND b.type = 5 WHERE cl.destination_Type = 4 AND cl.object_Id IN (the catalog's 40 scriveners): 2,783 create-list rows, 1,527 spells, one scroll each (ItemType 8192 Writable); spell is the scroll's SpellDID (int 28 of d_i_d), value its Value (int 19: 1, 5, 20, 100, 200, 1000 at I to VI, so 50, 250, 1,000, 5,000, 10,000, 50,000 pyreals at a scrivener's SellPrice 50, ACE Vendor.GetSellCost, Vendor.cs 577-585 @95ef426d), burden its Encumbrance (int 5: 30, or 10 for 22 rows), sellers each [scrivener wcid, create-list row id]. The name is the world's spell row; the line is the name less its numeral (I to VI), read at load. School and power are the SpellTable's (the dats), read where the rule runs: nothing here stands for them. Cassius' Ring of Fire (1785), the war picker's ring, has its scroll 7511 on no vendor's create list (destination 4): it is the loot's, as every VII (D4)
